subject: Food Science
title: Vitamin D and Sunlight
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Vitamin D and Sunlight.

hook.text: One billion people worldwide are vitamin D deficient. It's called the 'sunshine vitamin' because your skin makes it from UV light.

buildup.text: UVB radiation converts cholesterol in your skin to vitamin D3. It then travels to the liver and kidneys for activation.

discovery.text: Vitamin D regulates calcium absorption. Without it, bones weaken—rickets in children, osteoporosis in adults.

twist.text: Darker skin produces less vitamin D from sunlight—melanin blocks UVB. At northern latitudes, deficiency is nearly universal.

climax.text: Few foods contain vitamin D naturally—fatty fish, egg yolks, UV-exposed mushrooms. Fortified milk is most people's main source.

punchline.text: Your skin is a vitamin factory—but only in sunlight. Most of us don't get enough.

quiz.question: Why are people with darker skin more prone to vitamin D deficiency?
options: Melanin in darker skin blocks UVB radiation needed for vitamin D synthesis
